prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1331; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at the light when struck from behind by a third-party vehicle. Claimant reports neck strain and stiffness. No attorney on file; claimant is handling the claim directly. Photos requested from both drivers.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant describes neck pain beginning the morning after the accident, rated moderate, worse with turning the head. Claimant states they have not yet seen a physician. Advised claimant to get medical evaluation and keep all treatment receipts. Sent written summary of the claim process and a list of documents needed.

Entry 3: Reviewed police report. Officer noted both vehicles had visible rear and front damage consistent with the reported impact. Third-party driver admitted following too closely in the report. Liability appears clear. Requested repair estimates for both vehicles from approved shops.

Entry 4: Claimant returned call. Medical visit completed; diagnosis recorded as cervical strain with a recommendation for physical therapy and rest from heavy lifting for two weeks. Claimant asked how injury compensation is calculated. Explained the general process for evaluating bodily injury once treatment is complete and that no offer will be made until records are received. Requested signed medical authorization.

Entry 5: Received signed medical authorization and treatment records. Physical therapy sessions scheduled and in progress. Claimant reports improvement in range of motion but occasional headaches. Repair estimate for insured vehicle received and under review. Will follow up in two weeks for updated treatment status before evaluating the injury claim.
